newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Women meet to boost role in E. Europe democracies.
newsitem.headline: Women meet to boost role in E. Europe democracies.

text.p: Hundreds of leading women including U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton gather in Vienna on Wednesday aiming to boost the role of women in the new democracies of Central and Eastern Europe.

The three-day forum entitled "Vital Voices: Women in Democracy" is being sponsored and chaired by the U.S. ambassador to Austria, Swanee Hunt, and will involve women from the United States, western Europe and the former Soviet bloc.
Hunt said its main goal would be "to explore ways to strengthen the role of women in developing open democratic societies".

Among the delegates will be the European Union Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs, Emma Bonino, National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz, the Vice-President of the Czech senate, Jaroslava Moserova, and former Lithuanian Prime Minister Kazimiera Prunskiene.
The forum is the first major women's congress since the U.N. Fourth Women's Conference in Beijing in September 1995, which Clinton also attended, to the annoyance of the Chinese authorities.
Clinton, a high-flying lawyer, has been an outspoken critic of alleged human rights and population control abuses in China, as well as a strong advocate of women's rights.
According to U.N. statistics, only 28 women have been elected heads of state or government anywhere in the world this century. Women hold around 13 percent of the seats in the world's parliaments.

Hunt, a major financial contributor to U.S. President Bill Clinton's election campaigns, said the plan was to bring together women leaders to share expertise and develop an East-West support network to help build democracy in the region.
Over the three days, delegates will participate in workshops exploring leadership strategies in law, politics and business.

"Democracy without the full participation of women is a contradiction in terms. To reach its full potential, it must include all of its citizens," Clinton was quoted as saying in a release ahead of the event.

Hunt, whose posting to Vienna ends in October, has spearheaded a number of initiatives in the past four years to bring together women from war-ravaged areas of Central and Eastern Europe to discuss reconciliation.
Clinton arrives in the Austrian capital on Thursday and will visit the prestigious Vienna opera.
She is scheduled to address the forum on its last day and to meet Austrian President Thomas Klestil.
